messages:
alex (cycloapp): Hey team — after upgrading @redwood-inference/sdk from 1.3.7 -> 1.4.0 our Next.js production build fails. Local dev works but Vercel build/errors show bundler issues and auth failures in production. Error: `Cannot use import statement outside a module` and TS complains `Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood-inference/sdk'`

maria (support): thanks — can you paste the error log and your package.json + node version? are you using ESM (type: "module") or CJS? which bundler (webpack/next/vite)? any custom webpack config?

alex (cycloapp): Node 18.17, Next 13.5 (webpack), project is still CJS (no "type": "module"), using `require('@redwood-inference/sdk')`. package.json excerpt: 
```json
{
  "name": "cycloapp",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood-inference/sdk": "^1.4.0",
    "next": "13.5.2"
  }
}
```
Full build error from Vercel: 
```
> Build failed
/node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/esm/index.js:1
import {createClient} from './client';
^^^^^^
SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module

Also TypeScript: Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood-inference/sdk'. 'node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/esm/index.js' implicitly has an 'any' type.
```
I tried rerunning with `esModuleInterop: true` and `allowSyntheticDefaultImports` but still seeing issues in CI.

maria (support): got it. two likely pieces: (1) package exports map or published artifacts changed in 1.4.0 and bundlers are resolving to dist/esm instead of dist/cjs for CJS projects, (2) types might not have been included in the package. can you try a quick repro locally by creating a minimal repo? also immediate workaround: pin to 1.3.7 (`npm i @redwood-inference/sdk@1.3.7`) — does that restore your build?

alex (cycloapp): pinning restores build, yes. but we need a path forward — can't keep pinned forever. I can create a minimal repo but wanted to check known issues / recommended package.json layout for bundlers.

jon (devex): FYI — we've got an internal report about an exports-map regression introduced in 1.4.0 (RWF-521). the package's `exports` did not include a `require`/CJS target for the root entry, causing Node/webpack to resolve to the ESM file. quick diagnostics/patch you can try in your app (temporary): add a resolutions/postinstall script that rewrites node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/package.json `exports` to include:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
Also ensure `types` points to the declaration: "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts". That should make TS and CJS builds happy. we'll push an official patch.

jon (devex): another common gotcha: bundlers (esp. Vercel/webpack) sometimes prefer the `module` field or the esm entry; if your project is CJS, set `resolve.mainFields` to [ 'main', 'module' ] or explicitly alias `@redwood-inference/sdk` to the cjs file in webpack config: 
```js
resolve: {
  alias: {
    '@redwood-inference/sdk$': path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/cjs/index.js')
  }
}
```
And for Next/Vercel you can add a simple webpack override in `next.config.js` to force the CJS build.

alex (cycloapp): thanks — one more wrinkle: in production we saw 401s for a few requests after the upgrade. could bundling change cause auth headers to be stripped? logs show `Missing API key` in server logs in prod only.

maria (support): yes — bundlers/CI often replace `process.env.*` at build time. If your runtime expects `process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY` and the env isn't present during the build step (or is inlined to `undefined`), the server will fail at runtime with auth errors. ensure the runtime env var is set in Vercel/your deployment environment, not only during build. If using DefinePlugin/rollup replace plugin, check that it isn't accidentally removing the env or changing the variable name.

jon (devex): to reproduce quickly for us please: (1) create minimal repo with Next + CJS config, (2) set `@redwood-inference/sdk@1.4.0`, (3) include a tiny server-side API route that does: 
```js
const sdk = require('@redwood-inference/sdk');
const client = sdk.createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
await client.generate({prompt: 'hello'});
```
and (4) provide a failing build log or a reproducible zip / GitHub link. we can use that to run CI on our end. If you can't share code, a sanitized package.json + next.config + full error stack helps.

alex (cycloapp): i'll put a small repro on GitHub and share the link. tried the exports patch locally by editing node_modules and it worked (build + types OK). thanks, will attach repro.

kim (eng-platform): assigning to eng-platform to cut a 1.4.1 patch with corrected exports/types and add a unit test to our publish pipeline to cover CJS/ESM resolution. ETA: will try to ship a canary within 24h and a full patch release in 48h. maria — can you attach the repro when alex posts it and mark RWF-521 as high priority in the escalation?

deploy-bot: canary pipeline started for package @redwood-inference/sdk@1.4.1-canary.2024-04-xx — running integration smoke tests. :rocket:

maria (support): thanks all — alex please paste the GitHub link here and I'll attach it to the ticket. in the meantime pinning to 1.3.7 is the safe workaround and adding the webpack alias or postinstall rewrite will unblock CI. :thumbsup:
